transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Avalon Head of ML), Mark (Avalon Infra), Priya (Product), Tom (Security)

Summary: Quick Console + API demo focused on selecting open models from the catalog, how we benchmark them, and how compatibility matrices map to deployment choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer wants a short pilot and a cost/latency estimate. Security and VPC details discussed.

Topics: catalog search, model shortlist, bench runs, quantization/kv cache compatibility, routing fallbacks, SOC2/KMS, pilot logistics

00:00 Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. we'll try to keep this to under an hour, quick intro from our side then Samira will run through the Console and the API, show how you can pick open models and hook up a bench.
00:06 Lena: Thanks Jordan, quick note we're trying to finalize vendor shortlists this week so the timing is, uh, tight. we want to see a clear path to a pilot.
00:12 Jordan: Got it, that's helpful. Samira, take it away.
00:18 Samira: Cool. I'm going to share my screen, give me a sec. (screen share) Okay this is the Redwood Console home, you can see model catalog here, filter by task, architecture, quantization level, and hardware compatibility. For Avalon we'll likely look at several open LLMs — smaller quantized variants for latency-sensitive endpoints and larger ones for high-quality batch tasks.
00:45 Mark: When you say "hardware compatibility" does that include specific kernel/driver compatibility? we've had trouble with some 4-bit quant variants on older cards.
00:52 Samira: Yes, we map models to a compatibility matrix that includes kernel support, quantization profile (e.g., q4, q8), and recommended runtime kernels. sometimes the name of kernels gets munged in transcripts but basically we note whether a model has verified nvfuser or aten pathway on tested CUDA + specific driver ranges.
01:15 Lena: Are those compatibility checks automatic or manual? we have compliance steps that require us to know what was validated.
01:21 Samira: It's semi-automated — our onboarding bench runs smoke tests across hardware pools and we surface verified pass/fail; for private deployments we can run the same checks inside your environment as part of the pilot. we'll include the raw bench artifacts.
01:35 Priya: Walk us through how you compare models — what's in the benchmark sheet? latency only or quality metrics too?
01:41 Samira: Good question. Benchmarks we typically run include median and p95 latency at a few batch sizes, tokens/sec, memory footprint, and a small set of quality metrics (approx BLEU-like or task-specific evals) depending on the prompt set. the spreadsheet we share has tabs: hardware, model variant, quant settings, latency distribution, cost estimate per 1M tokens.
02:10 Jordan: Also we add a compatibility column so you can see whether the model will route to hosted, to dedicated, or require private due to kernel or privacy constraints.
02:21 Mark: About private deployment — what's the network setup? we need VPC peering and strict egress controls.
02:26 Jordan: For Redwood Private we support customer VPC with either a customer VPN or VPC peering; we can also do an on-prem package if air-gapped is required. Samira can share the network diagram later.
02:37 Tom: Security questions — KMS integration, key rotation, and audit logs. do you push logs to customer SIEM?
02:44 Samira: Yes, we have KMS/HSM integrations and can route audit logs to your SIEM. For SOC 2 we have attestations and for higher compliance we can provide architecture docs. we'll send the SOC2/ISO PDF and the KMS integration notes after.
03:00 Jordan: Let's jump to a shorter demo flow — picking a model and running a bench via the API.
03:07 Samira: On the console you can pick "Create bench" and either use our sample workloads or upload your prompt set. I'm going to demo a quick bench with a 200-sample prompt set. (starts demo) The API call looks like: POST /benchmarks with model_id, prompt_set_id, hardware_target. You can also do streaming results.
03:35 (crosstalk) Speaker 1: Sorry can you repeat the API endpoint?
03:38 Samira: Yeah, POST /v1/benchmarks, payload includes model, quant_profile, sequence_length distribution. response includes latency histogram and a CSV link with raw traces.
03:52 Lena: For our production use we have many short queries at high qps — how do you recommend we choose between a quantized smaller model and a larger float model?
04:00 Samira: It depends on your quality SLOs. our Optimize toolkit can suggest tradeoffs: if you require <100ms p95 we often recommend a q4 variant on dedicated with prefix caching and continuous batching optimized; if quality is paramount and p95 can be higher, a larger, less-quantized variant might be better. we'll show cost curves in the benchmark sheet.
04:28 Mark: What's the typical delta in token cost between hosted and dedicated?
04:32 Jordan: Ballpark: hosted covers maintenance/auto-scaling so per-token can be higher; dedicated reserved capacity reduces unit cost significantly at predictable throughput. we'll give a cost/latency table for your expected qps.
04:45 Priya: Can you do automatic fallbacks if the chosen model hits 429s or latency spikes?
04:51 Samira: Yes, smart routing allows fallbacks to compatible variants or to a cheaper region. you can set policies per route: latency-first, cost-first, or hybrid. we also have automatic canary rollouts for model versions.
05:10 Tom: For private data, do any tokens leave our network?
05:13 Jordan: With Private deployment, data stays in your VPC and we do not send inference payloads to our hosted plane; control plane still coordinates but can be configured to use your private control plane depending on the package. we'll detail that in the security doc.
05:30 Samira: I'm going to run a quick model shortlist — filter: task=clinical-notes, size<=10B, quantizable. Here we have three candidates: open-med-small-v2-q4, clinic-mix-6b-q8, and base-13b-fp16. The matrix shows that open-med-small-v2-q4 is verified on our A100 and Ampere-like pools with q4 kernels; clinic-mix-6b-q8 has some kernel warnings on older driver stacks (we mark as "partial pass"). base-13b-fp16 is best quality but needs more memory and likely dedicated.
06:15 Lena: Interesting. If you run our prompt set, can you show the p95 latency differences?
06:19 Samira: Yes — that's what the bench will return. I'm kicking off a quick smoke bench now, small batch sync. (bench runs) This will take a few minutes, I'll leave the console open and show the csv.
06:35 Samira: Meanwhile, a few gotchas: 4-bit quant can reduce quality on instruction-following prompts; we recommend running a small eval harness to catch major regressions. also KV-cache behavior differs by model — some models expose different caching semantics which change the effective latency on long conversations. we annotate that in the compatibility matrix as "KV cache: stable / partial / untested".
07:05 Mark: For long chat sessions, can caching be shared between endpoints?
07:09 Samira: You can share KV cache when the model and runtime support it; otherwise you may need per-session cache. in practice we see big wins with prefix caching for assistant workflows.
07:22 (brief silence while bench completes)
07:38 Samira: bench finished — uploading results. here's the CSV link in the console: /benchmarks/ff-20261002-avalon-quickbench.csv (note: link is illustrative). Quick numbers: open-med-small-v2-q4 p50 28ms p95 92ms at batch 1; clinic-mix-6b-q8 p50 34ms p95 140ms; base-13b-fp16 p50 78ms p95 260ms. memory footprints: q4 ~6.2GB, q8 ~8.1GB, fp16 ~26GB.
08:18 Lena: Those p95s for the small model look promising. can you also show cost per 1M tokens?
08:24 Jordan: In the bench sheet tab: open-med-small-v2-q4 is estimated $420 per 1M tokens on hosted, $210 on dedicated; clinic-mix-6b-q8 hosted $620, dedicated $310; base-13b-fp16 hosted $1,500, dedicated $680. these are illustrative — we'll run your exact traffic to refine.
08:50 Priya: Are the cost numbers accounting for prefix caching savings?
08:54 Samira: Yes, we present both cold-token and cached-token cost lines so you can model conversational savings.
09:05 Tom: On auditability — can we get per-request logs with token-level metadata?
09:09 Samira: Yes, with retention options; we can redact content if needed and push metadata to your SIEM. retention and access controls are adjustable.
09:22 Jordan: Let's talk pilot plan and timeline — given Lena's note about the vendor shortlist, we propose a 2-week pilot: you provide 2000 representative prompts, we run bench + small quality eval, then a short integration test in your staging with test keys.
09:35 Lena: That sounds reasonable; key constraint is we need the security docs before exec signs off.
09:40 Jordan: Understood. we'll send SOC2, KMS integration notes, and a sample MSA template. we'll also include a sample bench results workbook and our recommended shortlist.
09:54 (wrap up) Jordan: Quick recap of action items: we'll deliver cost estimates and run the bench on your set, Mark will share VPC details, Priya will confirm SLOs, Tom will list encryption requirements. Samira will upload the raw bench CSV and a walkthrough of the compatibility matrix.
10:10 Lena: Great, thanks everyone. we'll regroup once we have the docs.
10:15 Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot and the access keys. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional words were unclear (kernel names, exact file paths) — we'll attach the console links and bench artifacts in the follow-up email.
